reuse.why: No shared category selection is introduced; each month-wide action keeps its own query or loop and gets the template condition appended separately, and setZero gets a newly written variant of the filter.

duplication.why: The skip rule (hidden, hidden group, saved template) now lives in five places: three identical average queries, a new setZero query, and a JS predicate in copyPreviousMonth.

placement.why: Changes stay in budget/actions.ts where the actions live, but the eligibility rule is spread across SQL strings and a JS branch instead of one selection function in that module.

scope.why: Only the eligibility filters and one test change.

maintainability.why: The next change to which categories month-wide actions skip has to be made in five differently-written places, which already disagree in form (COALESCE vs plain g.hidden, v_categories vs categories, SQL vs JS).

bypasses_abstraction.where: The tree has no shared month-wide category selection to go around; the diff simply does not create one.

disguised_duplication.where: The same hidden/group-hidden/template rule is re-spelled per site: a COALESCE(g.hidden,0) query over v_categories in setZero, g.hidden = 0 over categories in the average actions, and goal_def != null in JS in copyPreviousMonth.

one_place.where: The rule is added separately to copyPreviousMonth (JS check on getBudgetData rows), setZero (new SQL), and set3MonthAvg/set6MonthAvg/set12MonthAvg (each own SQL).
